name: benchmark-bars
title: Benchmark bars
description: Prove a claim against the field: your customers' result beside the industry median for each metric, as paired bars with the multiple in words.
docs: Pass title, metrics ({ id, label, ours: { value, label? }, benchmark: { value, label? }, unit?, better, comparative? }), source (required) and methodHref. Each metric has its own scale: two bars (your customers in the foreground tone, the benchmark muted), both values written at the bar ends in tabular digits (keep them short: past 14 characters a value may wrap beside its bar, and the values never take more than 45% of a row, so a bar never collapses), and the multiple in words worked out from the same numbers ('7.4 times faster'; comparative picks the word when you win, otherwise 'higher' or 'lower'). With better: "lower" the shorter bar wins and a note says so; within 5 percent it reads 'in line with the median'; a result that trails is described as it is. Each metric is a figure whose caption reads the whole comparison to a screen reader. The bars are full on the server and on screen at load; a row still below the window grows once as it comes into view. Reduced motion and print show them at rest. labels sets the words.
